title: Red Team Handoff: SIEM Ingest & Evidence Automation
content:
Purpose:
This is a working handoff and coordination doc for external red-team or vendor pen tests where we need automated evidence collection, RBAC v2 validation, and immediate SIEM ingestion. Goal: make the triage and remediation loop fast and auditable, reduce manual evidence wrangling, and ensure SIEM parsers capture the fields needed for effective detection and SLA-backed response.

Scope (high-level):
- In-scope systems: Hosted API control plane, Dedicated control plane endpoints, Private deployment agents (VPC connectors), Console telemetry, auth/admin APIs.
- Out-of-scope: customer-managed on-prem models (unless customer explicitly included), developer local machines.
- Data types: auth events, admin role changes, model rollout API calls, token create/delete, container/instance lifecycle events, network egress alerts.

Assumptions and constraints:
- RBAC v2 rollout is active in prod canaries; some services still run legacy role checks (see notes).
- SIEM (Splunk) accepts syslog+HTTP bulk JSON; we have a dedicated ingest index for third-party tests.
- Evidence retention: short-term snapshots kept in GCS for 90 days; long-term artifacts in encrypted bucket with 7 year retention for compliance evidence.

Key objectives for this engagement:
1) Define minimal evidence set per finding type so vendor can export automatically.
2) Verify RBAC v2 enforcement (positive and negative tests) and capture audit trail for every step.
3) Ensure SIEM ingestion pipeline receives normalized events (audit schema) in <60s for priority issues.
4) Provide remediation playbook templates and automated verification steps to close findings rapidly.

Mapping: Finding type -> Evidence set (minimal)
- Privilege escalation (admin role bypass):
  - API logs for role_change POST/PUT (audit.trace_id, actor_id, target_id, before_roles, after_roles, timestamp)
  - Auth logs for actor session (session_id, ip, user_agent, mfa_flag)
  - RBAC policy snapshot (rbac_v2_policy_version, policy_hash)
  - Host/container snapshot (instance id, git_commit, docker_image, running processes)
- Data exfil / unauthorized read:
  - Access logs for resource (resource_id, action=read, response_size, requester_id, timestamp)
  - Network flow (src_ip, dest_ip, bytes, protocol) within retention window
  - SIEM alert correlation (if any) with matching trace_id
- Lateral movement / compromised service account:
  - Service account token issuance events (token_id, issuer, scopes, ttl)
  - Instance metadata access logs and IAM metadata calls

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields to include in every event):
- event_type (string)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- trace_id (uuid)
- actor_id (principal id / service account)
- actor_type (human | service | system)
- target_resource (resource namespace / id)
- action (string, e.g., role.change, auth.login, model.deploy)
- result (success | failure)
- ip_address (ipv4/ipv6)
- user_agent (string)
- request_id (provider request id)
- policy_hash (if relevant)
- raw_payload (base64 or truncated JSON for forensic copy)
Notes: Avoid proprietary field names; these map to Splunk sourcetypes and Lambda forwarders. At minimum include trace_id to correlate across services.

SIEM ingest patterns and parser guidance:
- Preferred transport: HTTP JSON POST to /ingest/thirdparty with header X-Test-Run: <id>. Backup: syslog over TLS to ci-collector-01.
- Indexing rules: set sourcetype=redwood:audit and tag=test-engagement.<id>.
- Recommended extraction fields: trace_id, actor_id, action, target_resource, event_type, timestamp.
- Parsers: use the provided Splunk props/config in linked repo. Example prop stanza: SHOULD extract trace_id as hex and map timestamp to _time.

Evidence automation plan (playbook):
1) Kickoff 
   - Verify engagement scope, test windows, blast radius, and allowed exploit types.
   - Agree on test-run id and create index in SIEM (owner: Security Ops).
2) Pre-test validation (2 hours before)
   - Snapshot RBAC policies (rbac_v2_policy_version -> gs://redwood-sec/evidence-snapshots/<test-id>/rbac.json)
   - Enable verbose audit for affected services (toggle from 30% to 100% for window).
   - Start background collector: gs://redwood-sec/collectors/ingest-agent v1.9 with test-run-id env var.
3) Live collection (during test)
   - Auto-tag events with test-run-id; ensure vendor has token to push to inflight endpoint.
   - If high-severity event occurs, open incident channel Slack #sec-redteam-<id> and trigger pager (SRE oncall).
4) Post-test consolidation (within 24h)
   - Consolidate event dump, policy snapshots, host images, and any proof artifacts into the encrypted evidence bucket.
   - Run automated correlation scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/security/siem-ingest-automation/scripts/correlate.sh <test-id>
   - Produce findings summary CSV and attach to JIRA template (JIRA-SEC-###).

Automation artefacts and locations (working):
- SIEM parsers and props: github.com/redwood-inference/security/splunk-props (branch: redteam-ingest)
- Collector agent: gs://redwood-sec/collectors/ingest-agent/v1.9/
- Correlation scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/security/siem-ingest-automation
- Evidence snapshots path: gs://redwood-sec/evidence-snapshots/<test-id>/
Notes: paths are environment-controlled; use service account sec-evidence-uploader@redwood-sec.

RBAC v2 validation checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm policy_version hash recorded pre-test and post-test.
- [ ] Run positive test cases (expected allow) for each admin action and capture event.
- [ ] Run negative test cases (expected deny) for a sampled non-admin user.
- [ ] Verify audit log contains both allow and deny events with trace_id.
- [ ] Validate that no bypass endpoints (legacy) were used; list exceptions.

Remediation and verification workflow (recommended):
- Create JIRA per finding (label: redteam-<id>, priority: P1/P2/P3)
- Attach minimal evidence set and correlation output.
- Assignment: Solutions Eng for code-level fixes, Infra SRE for config/infra, Product for policy decisions.
- Post-fix verification: automated smoke tests (see repo scripts) and RBAC smoke with 10 sample accounts.
- Closure: Security owner verifies SIEM shows expected deny/allow over a 24h window and evidence archived.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Finalize SIEM field mapping for model.deploy events (need enriched model_id and model_version fields).
- Confirm whether private deployment agent logs flow through the central collector or directly to customer SIEM.
- Add a small wrapper to the collector agent to optionally include env tags and policy hashes in every event.

Communication plan during engagement:
- Primary channel: #sec-redteam-<id> Slack (public channel for SRE + Security + Vendor liaison).
- Incident escalation: PagerDuty schedule -> sec-oncall -> engineering lead.
- Daily wrap: 15 minute quick-summary in #sec-ops at EOD with CSV of new findings.

Retention and compliance notes:
- Evidence snapshots for pen tests are encrypted at rest and access audited. Only sec-evidence-uploader and sec-audit group have write.
- Retention policy: 90 days hot, 3 years cold (encrypted), 7 years legal hold for regulated customers.

Appendix: Quick example audit event (newline-separated for copy/paste):
{
  "event_type": "role.change",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-18T14:02:31Z",
  "trace_id": "9f1b2e4a-6b7c-4d2a-ae9e-3b2f1a0c1234",
  "actor_id": "user:mchen@redwood.com",
  "actor_type": "human",
  "target_resource": "org:redwood:project:api-service",
  "action": "policy.update",
  "result": "success",
  "ip_address": "22.33.44.55",
  "user_agent": "redwood-console/2.1",
  "policy_hash": "sha256:abc123...",
  "raw_payload": "eyJzbmFwc2hvdCI6ICJkYXRhIn0="
}

Notes to reviewer: this is a working draft — expect gaps in the automation scripts list and a few TODOs above. Please comment inline or slack Maya (owner) with any blockers.
